lines: Look at your car tires. See those deep grooves in the rubber?
That pattern is called the tread. And it's doing a lot more than you think.
And today... I'm deleting it! Every single groove!
Look at that. A bald, round, sad rubber donut. Nobody wants you, tire.
And you're not even a tire anymore. You're a hockey puck with ambitions.
Now it starts to rain. And the car rolls onto a puddle.
Normally the grooves drain the water out from under the tire. Now there's nowhere for it to go.
So the water pushes the tire up like a wedge. Aquaplaning! The car can't steer or brake.
At that point, your car is sliding on a sheet of water. Like an ice rink, but on wheels.
A new tire pushes away about thirty liters of water every second at eighty kilometers per hour.
In most EU countries, the legal minimum tread is one point six millimeters.
Formula One slicks have no tread at all, until it rains. Then they switch to grooved tires.
And Formula One teams change tires for exactly this reason, every time the track gets wet.
So check your tread. Your whole car is literally standing on it.
So... what should I delete next?
